match.reason: No point in the bank covers market segmentation; the closest, market research for a new business, is about learning who will buy, not splitting a market into groups to target.

draft.title: Market segmentation
card: A market is all the people who might buy a product. Market segmentation splits it into smaller groups of customers who share something, so a business can target each group.
Demographic segmentation uses traits of people, such as age, gender, income or family size. Geographic segmentation uses where people live, such as city, region or climate.

Lifestyle segmentation uses how people live and what they value, such as interests and attitudes. Behavioural segmentation uses how people act as customers, such as how often they buy or how loyal they are.
A business can use more than one basis at once, such as age and region together.
draft.remember: Segmentation divides a market into groups with shared traits so each group can be targeted.

a.q: Which business is using geographic segmentation?
opts: A clothing chain selling heavy coats only in alpine towns
A gym offering cheaper memberships to students under 25
A bank targeting customers who value an outdoor life
A shop giving discounts to its most frequent buyers
a.why: Selling coats only in alpine towns divides the market by where people live. The student offer is demographic because it uses age. The outdoor life option is lifestyle, which is about values and interests, not place.
a.clue: Look for the option that sorts customers by where they live.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange gives a free loaf after ten visits on a loyalty card. Which basis of segmentation is she mainly using?
opts: Behavioural, as it rewards how often customers buy
Demographic, as it targets people by age and income
Geographic, as it targets people who live in Orange
Lifestyle, as it targets people who enjoy fresh bread
b.why: A loyalty card rewards a pattern of buying, which is customer behaviour. The bakery is in Orange, but the offer does not depend on where customers live. It also does not depend on their age or income, only on their number of visits.
b.clue: What does the free loaf depend on: who customers are or what they do?

a.best: A clothing chain selling heavy coats only in alpine towns

b.best: Behavioural, as it rewards how often customers buy
